The conclusion that mechanisms governing biological recognition largely apply to DNNs also requires narrower wording.

Necessary: The invariance metric needs stronger validation. Equations 5–7 compare mean activations across orientation sets, so a neuron can receive maximal similarity despite substantial variation within each set. Present these findings consistently as evidence compatible with a hypothesis, or provide controlled interventions supporting the stronger claims.

Necessary: Validate the interpretation of the invariance metric in Equations 5–8. Comparing regional mean activations can yield perfect similarity despite strongly orientation-dependent responses within each region. Additionally, requiring both regional means to exceed the activity threshold excludes neurons whose responses disappear under the distribution shift. Report retained neuron-instance counts and threshold sensitivity, and check whether the results persist with an analysis that measures variation across individual orientations.

Equation 4 produces an uncalibrated sum of sigmoid outputs, while Section 2.5 thresholds it at 10% of its maximum. These exceptions should be explained and the claims qualified.
